title: The Subharmonicon: undertones and polyrhythms from the 1930s, in a Moog semi-modular
intro: Moog Music released the Subharmonicon in 2020, after showing it as a limited instrument at Moogfest 2018. It takes two ideas from the 1930s. Oskar Sala’s Mixtur-Trautonium divided each note into subharmonics, lower notes in whole-number ratios to it; the Subharmonicon’s four subharmonic oscillators do the same to its two VCOs. Henry Cowell’s Rhythmicon, built by Léon Theremin, played rhythms in whole-number ratios; the Subharmonicon’s four rhythm generators divide its tempo the same way into two 4-step sequencers. Moog made it a semi-modular companion to the Mother-32 and DFAM, desktop or 60HP Eurorack.

timeline.name: Rhythmicon
timeline.text: Built by Léon Theremin for Henry Cowell: each key plays a repeating pulse at a rate in a whole-number ratio to the others, at the matching harmonic’s pitch.

timeline.name: Mixtur-Trautonium
timeline.text: Oskar Sala’s development of the Trautonium, adding subharmonic generators that divide each note into undertones; he used it for the bird sounds of Hitchcock’s The Birds (1963).

timeline.name: Moog Mother-32
timeline.text: Moog’s first desktop and Eurorack semi-modular: one VCO, a ladder filter and a 32-step sequencer.

timeline.name: Moog DFAM
timeline.text: The Drummer From Another Mother: a semi-modular analogue percussion synth with an 8-step sequencer, built to sit beside the Mother-32.

timeline.name: Moog Subharmonicon
timeline.text: Two VCOs, each with two subharmonic oscillators at /1 to /16, a ladder filter and two attack–decay envelopes; four rhythm generators stepping two 4-step sequencers, with quantising to equal or just tunings and a 32-point patchbay.

relatives.name: Moog Mother-32
relatives.text: The semi-modular the Subharmonicon was made to join: its ASSIGN output set to a clock can drive the Subharmonicon’s CLOCK input.

relatives.name: Moog DFAM
relatives.text: The percussion companion: the Subharmonicon’s CLOCK OUT, TRIGGER or SEQ CLK outputs can clock it.

relatives.name: Behringer Spice
relatives.text: A desktop semi-modular after the Subharmonicon, with the same two oscillators, four sub-oscillators and two four-step polyrhythmic sequencers, patched through a matrix.
